newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court bans rightist police union.
newsitem.headline: French court bans rightist police union.

text.p: A French court banned on Monday a police union linked to Jean-Marie Le Pen's ultra-rightist National Front party, ruling that its statutes did not make it a regular trade union.
The court in Evry near Paris was ruling in a suit brought against the Police National Front union by rival police unions after the FNP was created last November.

FNP got 7.45 percent of votes in a nationwide police union poll shortly after its creation. The single largest police union, FASP, which represents more than half the country's policemen, especially those in uniform, is left-leaning.
The ban against the FNP follows similar bans against recently-created National Front branches in the Paris transit authority and among prison guards.
Le Pen scored 15 percent of the vote in France's 1995 presidential elections.
